findings.message:
[P1] Keep production owner proof waits working with inline clocks

`hostedExecutionWait` now rejects every non-`SystemClock` clock without `sleep`, but production owner-proof clients in `src/host/owner-install-supersession.ts`, `src/host/owner-install-supersession-normal.ts`, `src/host/owner-install-future-recovery.ts`, and `src/host/owner-successor-acceptance-proof.ts` construct `GitHubApiClient` with inline real clocks (`{ now: () => Date.now() }`) and then call `nativeProof` which calls `readHostedExecution`. When GitHub exposes a completed repair job before its runtime metadata, the wait is entered, this throw is caught as `unavailable`, and the bounded metadata re-reads are skipped, so owner supersession or recovery can fail instead of completing that re-read. This depends on the metadata-lag scenario; those callers should use `SystemClock` or provide a `sleep` seam.

src/github/client-hosted-execution.ts:351-354

summary: Adds clock-based waiting and tests, but the fail-fast path breaks existing production clients that use inline real clocks without a sleep seam.

evidence: src/github/client-hosted-execution.ts:349-350 calls the injected clock sleep before falling back to a real timer.
src/github/client-hosted-execution.ts:351-354 throws immediately when a non-SystemClock clock has no sleep seam.
tests/github/hosted-execution-wait_test.ts:82-99 verifies clock sleep is used with its receiver and a seamless custom clock rejects without scheduling a timer.
